name: Heparin (unfractionated)
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Unfractionated heparin is cleared mainly by binding to cells and proteins rather than by the kidneys, so the US label gives no kidney dose change; full-dose therapy is titrated to coagulation tests. The label gives a starting dose for anticoagulating the hemodialysis circuit when the equipment maker gives none. Watch for heparin-induced thrombocytopenia and bleeding.
kidney_function_basis: Not applicable: dosing is by indication, weight and coagulation tests.

bands.recommendation: Full-dose IV: 5,000 units bolus, then 20,000 to 40,000 units/24 hours by infusion, adjusted to coagulation tests. Prophylaxis: 5,000 units SC 2 hours before surgery, then every 8 to 12 hours (label). No kidney dose adjustment in the label; dose by indication and coagulation tests (aPTT or anti-Xa for full-dose therapy).

hd: Circuit anticoagulation: follow the equipment maker's directions; if none, 25 to 30 units/kg, then 1,500 to 2,000 units/hour (label 2.9). Systemic doses: no kidney adjustment.
pd: No kidney dose adjustment in the label; dose by indication and coagulation tests (aPTT or anti-Xa for full-dose therapy).
crrt: No CRRT-specific dose in the label (2.9 covers extracorporeal dialysis generally: follow the equipment maker's directions). Use the unit's CRRT anticoagulation protocol; specialist input.
monitoring: aPTT (or anti-Xa) for full-dose therapy; platelet count (heparin-induced thrombocytopenia: stop if below 100,000/mm3 or new thrombosis); hemoglobin and signs of bleeding. Potassium in CKD: the label lists suppression of aldosterone synthesis (link to hyperkalemia is clinical extrapolation).

pediatric.approved_ages: Used in children; no adequate controlled pediatric studies, dosing from clinical experience (label 8.4). Use preservative-free heparin in neonates and infants.
pediatric.usual_dose: 75 to 100 units/kg IV bolus over 10 minutes, then infants 25 to 30 units/kg/hour (under 2 months average 28 units/kg/hour), children over 1 year 18 to 20 units/kg/hour; adjust to aPTT 60 to 85 seconds (label 2.4).
pediatric.neonates: Preservative-free formulation only (benzyl alcohol 'gasping syndrome'); infants under 2 months have the highest requirements (label).
pediatric.hd: Follow the equipment maker's directions or unit protocol for circuit heparin (label 2.9 gives an adult starting dose); specialist.
pediatric.crrt: No CRRT dose in label; unit protocol; specialist.
